I read this as a resolution problem with a misleading completion signal. My evidence B-H1 is five interviews with people who completed pages: they reported confusion about whether their claim was resolved. We did not interview abandoned users, so those interviews do not establish their experience or the extent of the problem.

I need to challenge the sponsor's proposed equivalence between page completion and eligibility approval. B-P1, our supplied fictional local rule, requires authorized human review of ambiguous claims; page completion has no eligibility meaning. B-P2 lets me approve routing and wording against that rule, but gives me no basis to invent eligibility criteria. I can sign off that distinction; I cannot certify language or disability access.

My proposal is a bounded fortnight intervention: human-review routing for ambiguous claims, clearer completion wording, resolution tracking, and a participatory check informed by an actual access consultation. The listed costs are 2 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 8 units, leaving one unit uncommitted. That excludes the separately priced assisted slot; its absence is a real unresolved limitation. I am not claiming these activities establish readiness or improve outcomes before we observe them.

Director, what authorized review capacity and escalation ownership can you commit within that scope, and what would your operational evidence require us to change? I request access advice on the proposed route and check before we decide whether any release is justified.

Can you obtain evidence of a named authorized reviewer, available review capacity and a workable handoff within the fortnight? Until then, I support documenting the bounded plan with no release. My policy signoff covers the stated routing constraint only, not eligibility decisions or access readiness.
